text: Where blue-green stands up a second full environment, a rolling update replaces a running service's instances gradually, inside the same environment.

Starting from four old instances, each step swaps one more for the new version. The load balancer routes to whatever's currently healthy -- there's never zero capacity, but there's also never a full standby copy sitting idle.

Two settings control how aggressive the rollout is. Max surge is how many extra instances can exist temporarily above normal. Max unavailable is how many can be down at once. A conservative rollout keeps unavailable at zero and surge small -- slow, but safe.

During the rollout, old and new versions genuinely serve traffic at the same time, for the whole duration -- which can be minutes, not an instant. For an AI app, that means two different model checkpoints can be live simultaneously, and the same question asked twice can get two different, both correct, answers.
Rolling updates skip blue-green's doubled cost, at the price of a visible side-by-side window. Next up: what to actually do when the new version turns out to be the problem -- rollback strategies.
